ar_coffee_cake_boulder.blurb: Coffee Cake Boulder is a single sandstone block on the north side of Fitzgerald Mountain in northwest Arkansas, holding ten boulder problems. Grades are a tight spread: six problems at V2 and four at V3, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate boulders who want a short, focused session rather than a big circuit. The block is on the trail's west side, a little beyond Coyote Cave. Some lines are on the tall side, but ledges like stair steps on the west face let you top out lower down if the full height feels like too much.

ar_coyote_cave_wall.blurb: Coyote Cave Wall is a small sandstone sport crag in the northern section of Fitzgerald Mountain, in northwest Arkansas. It holds ten routes, nine of them bolted and one trad line. The grades run from 5.8 up to a single 5.11, with the bulk sitting between 5.8 and 5.10, which makes it a reasonable stop for climbers working through the moderate range. Fitzgerald Mountain is still in early stages of climbing development, so expect a quiet, low-key outing rather than a busy cliff.

ar_north_wall.blurb: North Wall forms the north face of Stack Rock, a secluded sandstone crag in the Richland Creek area of north-central Arkansas. Its ten routes split evenly between sport and trad, from about 5.7 to the low 5.12s, with a few each at 5.9 to 5.10 and three in the 5.12 range. From the main cliff, walk left and circle the base; the trail the other way grows in heavily. Stack Rock wraps around in a crown shape, so some walls catch sun while others stay shaded through the day. The trail and cliff get overgrown in summer, so cooler months suit it best.

ar_heart_chamber_the.blurb: The Heart Chamber is a steep, concentrated wall at Stack Rock, a remote sandstone crag in the Richland Creek area of north-central Arkansas. Of its ten routes, eight are sport and two trad. It has an easy warm-up end near 5.8 and a hard end that tops out in the 5.12s, with most lines at 5.11 and 5.12, so it is mostly for strong climbers. Walk left along the cliff from the main face to find it. The wall is usually shaded until around midday, and some of the steeper lines keep dry in light rain.

ar_titanic_boulder.blurb: Titanic Boulder is a very large block on the West Side of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch in north-central Arkansas, carrying ten bolted and trad routes on sandstone. Eight are sport and two trad, spanning 5.8 to a single 5.13, with four at 5.10 and a pair at 5.11, so the middle grades are well served. The view from the top is among the best around. The West Side as a whole is a long wall that faces east and sits in shade for much of the day, which helps on warm afternoons. A marked side path leads to the block from the campsites.

ar_nasty_wall.blurb: Nasty Wall is a sandstone sport wall in Fern, a small creekside climbing area in northwest Arkansas where most climbs stay under about 50 feet. It has ten bolted routes between 5.8 and 5.11, concentrated at 5.10: six routes sit in that range, with one each at 5.8 and 5.9 and two at 5.11. It is reached by the Standard approach through the narrow corridor, then a left turn along the bluff, so allow some walking before you rope up.
